tasks.goal: Our release tool sorts tags with `compare`, and it orders 1.10.0 before 1.9.0 and puts 1.0.0-rc.1 after 1.0.0. Make `compare` follow SemVer 2.0.0 precedence exactly (spec section 11): major, minor and patch compare as numbers of any size (a tag can be longer than u64), a pre-release version has lower precedence than the same normal version, pre-release identifiers compare dot by dot (numeric ones as numbers, numeric lower than alphanumeric, a longer set wins when all earlier ones are equal), and build metadata is ignored. Return None for anything that is not a valid SemVer 2.0.0 string: no leading zeros in numeric fields or numeric pre-release identifiers, no empty identifiers, only [0-9A-Za-z-] in identifiers, no "v" prefix, no whitespace. Keep the signature.

tasks.goal: The sync client backs off by `retry_after`, but servers that send an HTTP-date make it give up. Make `retry_after` read a Retry-After field value as RFC 9110 section 10.2.3 defines it: either delta-seconds (digits only, at most the u64 range, else None) or an HTTP-date, with optional spaces or tabs around the value. For a date, return the seconds from `now_unix` until that date, and 0 when the date is in the past. RFC 9110 section 5.6.7 says a recipient must accept all three date formats: IMF-fixdate ("Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT"), the obsolete RFC 850 form ("Sunday, 06-Nov-94 08:49:37 GMT") and asctime ("Sun Nov  6 08:49:37 1994"). Return None for anything else, including impossible dates and times and zones other than GMT. Use no crate; keep the signature.

files.CONFIG.md:
# Configuration

## Port

The server reads its port from the config file (`port = 8080`) or from `APP_PORT`.
If a value is wrong, the server uses port 8080.

tasks.goal: Ops lost an hour because APP_PORT=80a silently fell back to 8080, and the file beat the environment. Fix `port` in src/config.rs: APP_PORT beats the file, and the file beats DEFAULT_PORT. An empty or blank value counts as unset, and surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Any other value must be a whole number from 1 to 65535 written with digits only (no sign, no hex); otherwise return BadPort naming the source of that value, and never fall back. A value that is never needed (the file's, when APP_PORT is good) is not checked. Then update CONFIG.md so it states this exact rule: the order, that empty means unset, the range 1 to 65535, and that a bad value makes the server refuse to start. Keep the types and the signature.

tasks.goal: Support staff can read customer passwords and tokens in the console, because `redact` only knows one key and breaks the line. Rewrite `redact` in src/redact.rs so that it hides the value of every `key=value` pair whose key is password, token, api_key, secret or authorization, matched in any case and only as a whole key (passwordless=, my_password_hint= and tokens= are other keys and stay as they are). A value ends at a space, tab, `&`, `;` or `,`, or the end of the line; a value in double or single quotes is hidden whole, quotes included. Also hide the token after "Authorization: Bearer " (any case). Replace each hidden value with `***` and keep every other byte as it was, UTF-8 included. Redacting a redacted line must change nothing. Keep src/lib.rs re-exporting `redact` and keep the signature.
